Sr3d.species_description: Sr3d5/2 STO, Sr3d3/2_STO, Sr3d5/2 SrCO3, Sr3d3/2_SrCO3
Sr3d.summary: The Sr 3d core level was fitted with two spin-orbit doublets, each comprising Sr 3d₅/₂ and Sr 3d₃/₂ components, using a Shirley background and symmetric SGL (sum of Gaussian-Lorentzian) line shapes. The primary doublet, assigned to SrTiO₃ (STO), exhibited binding energies of 132.51 eV (Sr 3d₅/₂) and 134.27 eV (Sr 3d₃/₂), with a constrained spin-orbit splitting of 1.74 ± 0.05 eV and a fixed area ratio of 3:2, consistent with theoretical expectations. A secondary doublet, attributed to SrCO₃, was resolved at 133.17 eV (Sr 3d₅/₂) and 134.86 eV (Sr 3d₃/₂), with identical spin-orbit splitting and area constraints, while its broader full width at half maximum (FWHM = 1.60 eV) reflected the more disordered chemical environment. The FWHM and Lorentzian contributions were linked within each doublet, and position offsets were fixed relative to the Sr 3d₅/₂ components to maintain physical consistency. Quantification of peak areas revealed that SrTiO₃ dominated the spectrum (~85% of total Sr signal), while the SrCO₃ contribution (~15%) indicated surface carbonation, a common artifact in perovskite oxides exposed to ambient conditions. The elevated chi-squared value, though high, reflected the complexity of the fit rather than poor model accuracy, as the constraints and peak shapes were carefully justified by the known chemistry of the system.

C1s.species_description: C1s C-C, C1s C-O, C1s C=O, C1s O-C=O
C1s.summary: The C1s core level spectrum was fitted with four singlet components using a Shirley background and a mixed Gaussian-Lorentzian line shape model. The dominant peak at 284.8 eV was assigned to adventitious C-C/C-H bonding, while a secondary component at 285.9 eV was attributed to C-O species, consistent with surface oxidation or organic contamination. Two additional peaks at 286.8 eV and 288.9 eV were assigned to C=O and O-C=O (carbonate) functionalities, respectively, with the latter suggesting the presence of SrCO3 on the SrTiO3 surface. All components were constrained to identical full-width at half-maximum values (1.35 eV) and Lorentzian-Gaussian ratios (10:90), while their binding energy positions were linked to the C-C reference peak with fixed offsets of +1.24, +2.50, and +3.60 eV for the C-O, C=O, and O-C=O species. The peak area analysis reveals that C-C species dominate the spectrum (87% of total carbon), with C-O contributing approximately 13%, while C=O and carbonate-related O-C=O components account for minor fractions (<2% combined), indicating that while the sample surface is primarily contaminated with adventitious hydrocarbon, the presence of the O-C=O peak provides evidence for carbonate formation consistent with SrCO3 precipitation on the oxide surface.

O1s.species_description: O1s oxide, O1s defect, O1s CO₃, O1s C-O
O1s.summary: The O1s core level spectrum was fitted with four distinct components using a Shirley background and singlet peak models with Lorentzian-Gaussian line shapes. The dominant component at 529.4 eV was attributed to lattice oxygen in the SrTiO3 matrix, while a secondary peak at 530.4 eV was assigned to oxygen-containing defects, likely oxygen vacancies or undercoordinated surface sites. Two additional components at 531.8 eV and 532.9 eV were identified as carbonate (CO₃²⁻) and C-O species respectively, confirming the presence of surface carbonation consistent with SrCO3 formation. The defect peak position was constrained to remain 1.50 eV above the oxide component to maintain chemical consistency. The oxide species dominated the spectrum with an area of 25,776 counts (approximately 65% of the total), while defect oxygen contributed 10,372 counts (26%), and carbonated species (CO₃ and C-O combined) accounted for only 1,747 counts (4%). This composition indicates that while the bulk of the sample retains the SrTiO3 stoichiometry, significant surface oxidation and defect formation have occurred, with minor carbonate contamination likely arising from atmospheric CO₂ exposure during sample handling or storage.
